#### 1. spinocerebellar ataxia type 28  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.472)

Loss-of-function mutations in both SPG7 and AFG3L2 impair mitochondrial protein homeostasis, leading to the development of spastic paraplegia (HSP7) and spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA28), respectively. The shared disruption of mitochondrial protein quality control pathways creates a converging mechanism for these neurodegenerative diseases.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that the causal variants for HSP7 and SCA28 affect entirely independent cellular pathways with no overlap in mitochondrial protein homeostasis, or if these pathways are shown to be functionally distinct and non-interacting, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs144962494 (SPG7 variant with high frequency in some populations))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of mitochondrial protein homeostasis in HSP7 and SCA28 could lead to the development of therapies targeting this pathway, potentially benefiting patients with either disease. Interventions aimed at improving mitochondrial function or protein turnover could offer a common therapeutic strategy.
